react_result.final_narrative_text: Analysis of eight differentially abundant metabolites identified two independent, cross-paradigm-consistent biological signals. The strongest network-level hit was prostaglandin and thromboxane biosynthesis: mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked 'Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate' first among all pathways (p=0.0054) with a perfect 3-of-3 metabolite overlap, driven directly by the input thromboxane A₂ (KEGG:C02198, CHEBI:15627). Arachidonic acid (the canonical substrate of PTGS1/COX-1 and PTGS2/COX-2) appears as the pathway context compound, and the thromboxane synthase reaction (R02377) mediates the terminal conversion. The second signal emerged from RaMP multi-database ORA: the selenium atom (KEGG:C01529, CHEBI:27568) significantly enriched three WikiPathways entries — Ferroptosis (WP:WP4313, FDR=0.0011, fold enrichment 1351), the Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15, FDR=0.0021, fold enrichment 487), and Pluripotent stem cell differentiation (WP:WP2848, FDR=0.0007, fold enrichment 4157). Selenium is a cofactor for glutathione peroxidase (GPX family) and thioredoxin reductase, enzymes that directly suppress ferroptosis by repairing lipid peroxides; perturbation of selenium homeostasis therefore collapses this ferroptosis-suppression mechanism. The remaining four input compounds (bromide, D-glucose, methimazole, benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide, beta-mercaptoethanol, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl) did not resolve to curated human pathway members in either ORA or mummichog, indicating either annotation gaps or biological noise for these structures.
